sections.title: Letter name and sound
paragraphs: The name of this letter is (ű) /yː/. It makes the sound you hear in (űr) /ˈyːr/, which means space, cosmos. This letter has only one sound in standard speech.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Push your tongue high and forward near your front teeth. Pucker your lips forward into a small tight circle. Let your vocal cords vibrate to make a voiced sound. A voiced sound makes your throat shake. Hold that shape steady without moving your mouth.

sections.title: Reading this letter
paragraphs: This letter always keeps the same long vowel sound in every position. A double acute accent mark gives it this length. You hear it at the start of (űr) /ˈyːr/ and inside (tűz) /ˈtyːz/.

sections.title: Mistakes to avoid
paragraphs: Do not make a diphthong like the sound in the English word few. A diphthong glides from one sound to another. Keep your lips pushed forward and steady. Do not say the back vowel sound heard in the English word boot. Keep your tongue pushed fully forward.
